record.original_question: For the Wang-Swendsen-Kotecky (WSK) dynamics for zero-temperature Potts colorings on periodic lattices, for which lattice sizes n is the dynamics ergodic in the currently unresolved cases q=4 on an n x n periodic triangular lattice and q=3 on an n x n Kagome lattice?

evidence.quote: All other cases are open (to the best of my knowledge). In particular, we would like to know for which values of n (if any) the WSK dynamics is ergodic for q = 4 on an n x n periodic triangular lattice, or for q = 3 on an n x n Kagome lattice.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple graph and let q ≥ 2 be an integer. A proper q-coloring of G is a map σ : V → {1, 2, …, q} such that σ(u) ≠ σ(v) for every edge {u, v} ∈ E. The Wang–Swendsen–Kotecký (WSK) dynamics on the set of proper q-colorings of G is the following Markov chain: at each step, pick uniformly at random a pair of distinct colors {a, b} ⊂ {1, …, q} and a connected component C of the subgraph of G induced by the vertices colored a or b; with probability 1/2 swap the colors a ↔ b on every vertex of C (otherwise leave the configuration unchanged). The chain is said to be ergodic if its transition graph on the set of proper q-colorings is connected (equivalently, every proper q-coloring is reachable from every other).

Consider the following two families of graphs, each with fully periodic (toroidal) boundary conditions:

(a) The n × n triangular lattice T_n, i.e. the Cayley graph of (ℤ/nℤ)² with generators {(1,0), (0,1), (1,1)}, with q = 4.

(b) The n × n kagome lattice K_n (the line graph of the n × n honeycomb lattice on the torus), with q = 3.

For each of these two families, determine precisely the set of positive integers n for which the WSK dynamics on the set of proper q-colorings of the corresponding graph is ergodic.
artifact.category_tag: Markov chain ergodicity for Potts antiferromagnets
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results have appeared: non-ergodicity of WSK has been proved for the 3-state Potts antiferromagnet on symmetric subsets of the kagome lattice with fully periodic boundary conditions (Mohar–Salas, arXiv:1002.4279), and for the zero-temperature 4-state Potts antiferromagnet on triangulations T(3L, 3M) of the torus. More recent work (arXiv:2206.13126) establishes ergodicity on broader classes of quadrangulations and Eulerian triangulations but does not cover the triangular or kagome lattices in full generality. A complete characterization of the set of n for which WSK is ergodic in cases (a) and (b) does not appear to be established.

status_evidence.title: On the non-ergodicity of the Swendsen-Wang-Kotecky algorithm on the kagome lattice
status_evidence.snippet: this algorithm is not ergodic for symmetric subsets of the kagome lattice with fully periodic boundary conditions
status_evidence.claim: Non-ergodicity established for certain kagome cases, but not a full characterization in n.

status_evidence.title: Ergodicity of the Wang–Swendsen–Kotecký algorithm on quadrangulations and Eulerian triangulations
status_evidence.snippet: WSK ergodic for q ≥ 4 on any quadrangulation of the torus of girth ≥ 4, and q ≥ 5 (resp. q ≥ 3) on Eulerian triangulations with specific properties
status_evidence.claim: Newer ergodicity results don't fully resolve q=4 triangular or q=3 kagome cases.

status_evidence.title: Height Representation, Critical Exponents, and Ergodicity in the Four-State Triangular Potts Antiferromagnet
status_evidence.snippet: WSK algorithm for zero-temperature 4-state Potts antiferromagnet on triangulations T(3L,3M) of the torus is not ergodic
status_evidence.claim: Non-ergodicity is known in a subfamily of n for q=4 triangular case.
